text:
Miguel: Heads-up — cost spike this morning on us-west1 preemptibles, saw 2.8x token cost on several jobs. Thinking we should tweak the bid mix and warm-buffer behavior. Anyone free to sync quick?
Aisha: saw that too. Most of the surge looks like spot price churn + a couple of AZs trimming capacity. Jobs drained and moved zones, increased egress.
Priya: timeline? I have logs from the allocator. Prices started spiking ~06:05 PT and we saw 15% interruption rate for 8s instances over 12 mins.
Sam: is this related to the new auto-scale rule we rolled last week (burst=on) that spins up ephemeral spot GPUs in price-optimized pools?
Miguel: yeah likely. Price-optimized got cheap but volatile. When AZ prices jumped, our scheduler rebalanced and triggered cold starts in other zones -> more drains + network transfer.
Liam: suggestion: switch default mixing to capacity-optimized for production critical pools, keep price-optimized as overflow for non-latency workloads. We should also cap spillover concurrency to avoid cascade.
Aisha: agree. For Dedicated-like tails we should prefer capacity-optimized: fewer evictions even if slightly more expensive. For batch/long jobs keep price-optimized.
Priya: can we implement a fast-fail fallback to smaller model quantized variant on eviction instead of rescheduling across zones? That would save egress and reduce coldstarts.
Sam: +1. We have a `fallback_profile` in route config already but it's not enabled for many routes. We can enable for priority routes, have it return `model-v2-8q` instead of full `model-v2` for 60s after eviction.
Miguel: nice. Also let's add a small warm-buffer of on-demand or reserved grams per region — like 1-2 nodes per AZ — to absorb short spikes. Cost of that buffer < cost of repeated cross-zone transfers.
Liam: math check: 2 nodes * 3 AZs * $2/hr = $12/hr, versus a single cross-zone coldstart + egress + regen = >$30/hr during churn. Seems worth it.
infra-bot: alloc-1234: detected high interruption rate in us-west1-a. Current pool mix: 70% price-opt, 30% capacity-opt. Evictions: 18 in last 15m.
Priya: infra-bot stats are helpful. Plan: 1) flip critical pools to capacity-optimized (gradual over 10m), 2) enable `fallback_profile` for priority routes, 3) add 2-node warm-buffer per AZ, 4) throttle spillover to 20 concurrent rebalances. Anyone want to own the rollout?
Aisha: I can own the rollout steps 1 and 4, I'll coordinate with autoscaler.
Sam: I'll patch route config for `fallback_profile` and add the conditional TTL.
Liam: I'll take warm-buffer and cost projection, and add it to ops runbook with an escape hatch to flip back.
Miguel: sweet. Please keep changes canaryed in us-west1-beta (1 AZ) before full flip. Use 30-minute observability window and set alert if token cost >1.5x baseline or eviction rate >5% for 10m.
Priya: note for the scheduler: prefer shotgun placement across AZs only if budget allows. Add a scoring penalty for cross-AZ kills to discourage transfers during price churn.
Aisha: good call. Also adding small jitter to scale-up timing helps avoid synchronized coldstarts. I'll add random 0-20s delay to the burst path.
Sam: pushing config now to canary namespace. Will post diffs.
Miguel: thanks team. After canary, let's regroup in 40m. :thumbsup:
Sam: diff posted: https://internal/redwood/configs/allocator/1865000123 (contains `fallback_profile` changes and spill throttle).
Liam: putting cost calc in docs: https://internal/redwood/ops/warm-buffer-costs — will update with numbers and rollback steps.
infra-bot: deploy:config-canary to us-west1-beta started at 1865000450, status: in-progress.
Priya: monitoring dashboard linked: https://internal/redwood/dashboards/spot-evictions — keeping eyes on eviction, coldstart latency, and egress.
Miguel: perfect. If canary stable at +30m we rollout remainder. If not, revert to current mix and re-evaluate.
Aisha: noted. I'll watch autoscaler logs and call if anything weird.
Sam: canary finished — no spike in egress, eviction rate down from 15% -> 4% in canary AZ. Rolling to remaining AZs now.
Miguel: excellent, thanks. Follow-up: we should document recommended pool mixes by workload class (SLO-critical, interactive, batch) and put examples in runbook.
Liam: I'll draft that and share tomorrow.
Miguel: ok closing this thread for now. Great work. :tada:
